competitors.name: SGS (independent inspection, sampling and assay)
competitors.what_they_do: Global inspection and testing major with a commodities and minerals division that runs independent sampling, weighing, sample prep and assay for concentrates, scrap and, from my background knowledge, battery materials and black mass. UNVERIFIED this session: the site returned 403 and the search budget was exhausted. This is the most likely incumbent to already offer black-mass sampling plus assay, though probably under generic ISO-style or contract-specific protocols and not a Gy/TOS-based variance-certified referee product.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Public company; roughly CHF 6-7bn annual revenue (background knowledge, not verified this session)

UNVERIFIED: the group homepage I fetched had no black mass mention, and a guessed black-mass URL returned 404.

competitors.name: Alex Stewart International
competitors.what_they_do: Independent commodity inspection, sampling and assay group. I fetched the site: it lists lab testing of ores, concentrates, minor metals, PGMs, ferro-alloys and 'recycled scrap metal', with no explicit black-mass or battery-scrap page. It is a natural umpire-lab candidate for black mass disputes and a likely channel partner or competitor.

competitors.what_they_do: Large mining and commodities assay lab group. The battery-materials page I guessed returned an error page, so nothing about black mass is verified. It is the type of lab that would run the assay leg of a referee scheme, and is more likely a partner than a competitor.

white_space: Provisional, because the research was severely constrained: the session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted before any search ran, and the direct fetches of incumbent sites returned 403, 404 or no relevant content. Nothing below is web-verified. Likely unserved: (1) A sampling-variance-certified referee product, meaning a Gy/TOS-based protocol with a stated sampling variance, heterogeneity characterisation (variography, sampling nomogram) and a binding-settlement clause. Inspection majors sell 'independent sampling and assay' as a commodity service, but I found no evidence that they publish or guarantee sampling uncertainty for black mass. (2) On-site, containerised, inert-atmosphere sample prep at the recycler or gigafactory gate. Black mass is being pushed toward hazardous-waste treatment in the EU, which makes shipping bulk samples to distant labs harder. (3) Tying lot-level sampling data to EU Battery Regulation material-recovery and recycled-content documentation. The main risk is that SGS, Bureau Veritas/Inspectorate, Intertek or Alex Stewart already offer black-mass sampling and umpire assay and would call this an existing service. The whole wedge depends on their protocols being meaningfully worse than TOS practice, which is unproven and is exactly what the free duplicate-sampling study would test.
evidence_of_demand: None verified this session. The search budget was exhausted before any query ran, and the fetches of RFPs, forums or competitor pricing yielded nothing usable. Background-knowledge indicators only, which I could not confirm: the EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1542/oj, my fetch returned empty) sets recycling-efficiency, material-recovery and recycled-content requirements that force mass-balance documentation. Black mass is widely traded on payables tied to Ni/Co/Li assay, and umpire-lab clauses in offtake contracts are common in metals trading, which suggests sellers and buyers already pay for third-party assay. The claim of 5-15% between-party assay differences and the willingness to pay $1.5-4k per lot comes from the idea file itself and is unvalidated. Before building, validate with 5-10 conversations with scrap desks and recyclers, and by checking whether existing supply contracts already name an inspection company as umpire.
kill_reason: n/a. The evidence does not support a kill, but it does not support confidence either. No verified dominant incumbent offers a TOS-rigorous, variance-certified black mass referee product, but the research could not rule out that the major inspection companies already sell black-mass sampling and umpire assay. Treat this as 'gap, unverified'. Rerun the existence check with web search budget restored before committing capital.
sharper_angle: Do not compete head-on with SGS, Bureau Veritas or Intertek as a fourth inspection company, and do not lead with the $40-60k station. Sell 'sampling uncertainty' as the product, aimed at the party who loses on payables. (1) Start with the free duplicate-sampling study of 10 lots, which tests the premise of a 5-15% between-protocol bias cheaply and yields the sales evidence. (2) Package the output as a heterogeneity and sampling-variance audit (Gy nomogram, variography, duplicate-sample bias checks) plus a published referee protocol and a two-line contract clause that names a sampling variance limit. Sell it to gigafactory scrap desks and dismantlers, who are paid by assay and have the most to gain. (3) Position the protocol as the standard the inspection majors and umpire labs run, licensing or certifying their sampling crews and the recyclers' own, so the majors become channel partners and not rivals. (4) Add containerised gate-side prep only after a paying anchor customer, and target the EU hazardous-waste shipping constraint as the reason for on-site sample prep. (5) Feed the lot-level sampling data into EU Battery Regulation material-recovery and recycled-content reporting to make the service recurring and compliance-driven. Pick one corridor first, for example Germany and Poland scrap to hydromet recyclers.
